name: Hamming Radius of Majority
details: The class is realized on its $n$ ordinary coordinates and one majority coordinate.
proof: For any proposed center, complementing its ordinary-coordinate trace gives a class member that differs on all n ordinary coordinates, so radius at least n is necessary. Conversely, take the center with all ordinary coordinates equal to 1 and majority coordinate 0. A class member with ordinary subset A has distance n-|A| plus at most one for its majority bit; this is at most n. Hence the radius is exactly n.
